messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: unusual auth failure spike (401) from edge-proxy eu-west-1. Rule: proxy-auth-401-rate. Count=12k in 6m, 3sustained sources. AlertID=ALRT-20251104-09. :rotating_light:
oncall-rosa: I'm oncall, looking. grabbing logs and context.
eng-sre-eli: Seeing repeated requests to /v1/generate and /v1/auth with same User-Agent and identical X-Trace. Source IPs cluster around 45.32.11.9 and 45.32.11.10. Spike start ~2025-11-04T09:12Z. Requests contain suspicious header `x-debug:true`.
sec-anna: Suggest immediate block at edge and disable any external log forwarders to S3. Possible scraping of session tokens in logs. Also want to rotate the `log-forwarder-prod` service keys.
oncall-rosa: blocking IPs at edge now. tagging SOC and legal.
infra-ops: executing WAF rule update, applying block rules to fastly/edge:```
# fastly/edge - add block rule
fastly waf rule create --service edge-proxy --name block-45-32-11-9 --match "client.ip==45.32.11.9" --action block
# confirm
fastly waf rule get --service edge-proxy --name block-45-32-11-9
```
infra-ops: Block deployed, confirmed SYN/HTTP traffic from 45.32.11.9 now blocked at edge. 401 spike dropped by ~70% in last 90s.
incident-bot: Alert suppressed for ALRT-20251104-09 per mute by infra-ops.
pg-sarah: Found a staging->external S3 forwarder config still pointing to `s3://external-logs-prod-archive`. The `log-forwarder-prod` svcacct showed recent access at 2025-11-04T08:58Z. Need rotation.
eng-sre-eli: grep of rotated logs shows token-like strings appearing in a handful of log files that were forwarded. Not all look PII but could include session ids.
sec-anna: Action items: 1) keep block in place 2) disable log-forwarder pipeline to external bucket 3) rotate AWS keys for `log-forwarder-prod` svcacct and update KMS secrets 4) run quick audit for any S3 objects with leaked keys/tokens 5) notify customers if exfiltration confirmed.
oncall-rosa: disabling forwarder now.
infra-ops: disabled external forwarder, put pipeline in paused state.
pg-sarah: svcacct details: user=log-forwarder-prod, access-key=AKIAEXAMPLE12345 last-used=2025-11-04T08:58Z. Marking key for immediate rotation.
legal-bob: Preliminary ask: preserve logs and evidence, do not delete anything until SOC/legal confirms. If customer data confirmed, we need timeline + disclosure plan.
cust-success-james: Monitoring CS queue. No inbound tickets yet. Drafting a short non-alarming notice if needed.
sec-anna: I'll rotate keys now. Plan: create new access key, update secret in KMS, redeploy forwarder with new key, revoke old key. Pseudocode:```
# create new key
aws iam create-access-key --user-name log-forwarder-prod
# update secret
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id prod/log-forwarder --secret-string '{"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID":"NEWID","AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY":"NEWSECRET"}'
# restart forwarder
kubectl rollout restart deployment/log-forwarder -n infra
# revoke old
aws iam update-access-key --user-name log-forwarder-prod --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE12345 --status Inactive
```
infra-ops: New key created and pushed to SecretsManager, redeployed, forwarder currently in read-only / internal-only mode.
eng-sre-eli: Re-run search for other leaked credentials: `grep -R "AKIA" /var/log/* || true` — nothing else obvious. Also started a scan for bearer tokens pattern in forwarded S3 objects.
pg-sarah: Confirmed forwarder now only writes to `s3://internal-logs-sandbox` while we validate; external bucket ACL moved to private and access logs disabled.
sec-anna: Results so far: few forwarded files contained obfuscated session ids, no full tokens confirmed in exported files. Still doing deeper pattern match and sampling.
legal-bob: Keep SOC and compliance in the loop. Preserve snapshot of external bucket and chain of custody.
oncall-rosa: Customer impact assessment: 0 verified customer incidents so far. CS prepared message template if needed. We're keeping the incident open for 24h monitoring.
cust-success-james: Template ready, will hold until SOC ok.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (edge block + forwarder paused + keys rotated). Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Incident owner: oncall-rosa.
eng-sre-eli: Will run retention grab and a quick audit job:```
# snapshot objects
aws s3api list-objects --bucket external-logs-prod-archive --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,LastModified:LastModified}' > /tmp/snapshot.json
# sample download
aws s3 cp s3://external-logs-prod-archive/somefile.log /tmp/sample.log
grep -E "(session|token|AKIA)" /tmp/sample.log | head -n 50
```
sec-anna: Good. Preserve /tmp/snapshot.json to evidence store when done.
legal-bob: Agreed. Keep all copies and provide MD5 checksums.
oncall-rosa: Thanks all — great quick work. I'll close after 24h with final postmortem if no new findings. :thumbsup:
infra-ops: noting runbooks updated with a quick checklist for log-forwarder rotation.
eng-sre-eli: will follow up with a short write-up for runbook.
sec-anna: leaving SOC watch for 24h.
cust-success-james: ping me if we need to escalate customer comms.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed (monitoring window).
